source.title: Spontaneous symmetry breaking and Goldstone modes for deep information propagation
source.authors: Nabil Iqbal; T. Keller; Yue Song; Takeru Miyato; Max Welling

record.tranche_reason: The paper compares training outcomes for deep equivariant and generic networks, but uses a different architecture and reports test accuracy rather than training classification error.
record.gate_note: The paper reports test accuracy on Fashion-MNIST and MNIST for deep MLPs, plus sequence-task results. The MLP results bear on deep-network trainability, but do not measure training error on CIFAR or corrupted/random labels. Recurrent-task results do not test the listed versions.
record.test_reason: The initialization-scale sweeps bear on V4 in a new setting: 100-layer radial-tanh MLPs. At a fixed training budget, learning depends on initial weight scale, with signal and Jacobian analyses explaining the dependence. Test accuracy does not establish training-error claims in V1 or V3.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is accurate. The authors conclude that internal equivariance and spontaneous symmetry breaking provide protected information channels, improve deep-network trainability and recurrent memory, and permit training 100-layer networks without normalization or skip connections. They describe the practical benchmark evidence as preliminary.
record.recipe_differences: The study trains equivariant networks with symmetry-preserving layers and compares them with generic networks; it does not reproduce the listed recipes for training classification error.
record.method_sensitivity: The reported MLP training advantage depends on equivariance and the symmetry-broken weight-scale regime; the paper also varies group, depth, and dataset.

fits_no_version.finding: At fixed initialization, O(4) equivariant MLP test accuracy does not degrade over the tested depths, whereas generic MLP accuracy degrades.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Internal equivariance can preserve fixed-budget test performance as MLP depth increases without normalization or skip connections.

fits_no_version.finding: Equivariant recurrent models improve variable-delay copying and permuted sequential MNIST performance relative to generic recurrent baselines.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Internal equivariance can improve long-sequence memory and prediction in recurrent networks.

record.problems: For the relevant MLP results, the text gives figure descriptions rather than numeric accuracy values. The datasets are MNIST and Fashion-MNIST, and the reported measure is test accuracy rather than training error. The authors call the practical results preliminary.
record.rows_left_out: No separate numeric MLP results are stated in the text beyond the figure-only comparisons represented by R1–R5. Recurrent copy-task and permuted sequential MNIST results concern sequence modeling rather than the classification-error behavior in the claim.

untested.parts: Near-zero training classification error in large convolutional networks on CIFAR-10/100, including corrupted labels and the stated recipe exceptions.
Teacher-student ReLU optimization, spurious minima, and the effect of extra student neurons.
Training-error degradation in plain batch-normalized convolutional networks, identity-shortcut comparisons, longer training, and the specified initialization exceptions.

Direct training-speed curves across initializations; activation-function comparisons; orthogonal versus Gaussian weights; and 10,000-layer convolutional training. Protection of one Jacobian component does not establish preservation of the entire gradient spectrum.
Learning-rate stability thresholds, curvature trajectories, catapult recovery, edge-of-stability dynamics, and divergence.
Controlled batch-normalization comparisons, higher-learning-rate tolerance, and Fixup.

missing.what: Generic-model initialization sweep near the critical region: only modest performance gains occur near the transition, while a nonzero order parameter away from it is insufficient.

MNIST initialization sweeps reproduce the equivariant learning onset and poor generic-model performance. The record's assertion that no additional MLP comparisons require recording overlooks this separate dataset.

record.verdict_notes: The protected channel follows from equivariant architecture; initialization selects its active regime. These results do not show that initialization alone reproduces the architectural advantage. Unreadable exact figure values do not prevent using qualitative effects explicitly stated in captions.

versions.untested_parts: CIFAR-10/CIFAR-100 training error, corrupted or random labels, model size, early stopping, and regularization.
Two-layer ReLU teacher-student problems, spurious local minima, and student width relative to teacher width.

Plain versus residual networks, training error as depth increases, and the specified ImageNet/CIFAR-10 settings. Deep equivariant networks without architectural stabilizers are studied, but their test-accuracy results do not measure the version's stated behavior.
Activation-matched initialization schemes, signal and gradient preservation across depth, orthogonal versus Gaussian weights, and 10,000-layer convolutional networks.
Learning rates above stability thresholds, loss and curvature dynamics, and divergence.
Batch normalization comparisons and Fixup residual networks.

rows.subject: U(1) equivariant model
rows.operation_detail: Trained for 5 epochs while varying weight scale; test accuracy reported.
rows.note: The text says equivariant-model training appears to begin in the symmetry-broken phase; exact plotted values are not stated.
rows.check: The caption explicitly reports learning beginning in the symmetry-broken initialization regime. Exact accuracy values remain unreadable, but the qualitative initialization effect is stated.

rows.subject: Generic (non-equivariant) model with the same nonlinearity
rows.operation_detail: Trained for 5 epochs while varying weight scale; test accuracy reported.
rows.note: The paper describes training of non-equivariant models as poor; exact plotted values are not stated.
rows.check: This row covers mostly poorly performing initialization scales. Figure 10 separately resolves the generic model's critical region; poor performance in Figure 3 alone cannot establish whether an appropriate initialization helps. The generic controls for the two panels should also be distinguished.

rows.subject: O(4) equivariant model
rows.operation_detail: Trained for 5 epochs while varying weight scale; test accuracy reported.
rows.note: The text says equivariant-model training appears to begin in the symmetry-broken phase; exact plotted values are not stated.
rows.check: The stated onset of learning across initialization scales bears on V4 despite the absence of exact plotted values.

rows.subject: O(4) equivariant model
rows.operation_detail: Trained at fixed initial weight variance while varying number of hidden layers; test accuracy reported.
rows.note: The authors state that O(4) performance does not degrade with depth; plotted values are not given numerically.
rows.check: This compares depth at one fixed initialization, without an initialization comparison. It measures test accuracy in equivariant MLPs rather than V3's training-error comparison in plain and residual convolutional networks. Add the four-epoch training budget.

rows.subject: Generic (non-equivariant) model
rows.operation_detail: Trained at fixed initial weight variance while varying number of hidden layers; test accuracy reported.
rows.note: The authors state that generic-network performance degrades with depth; plotted values are not given numerically.
rows.check: Test-accuracy degradation with depth does not establish V3's training-error degradation. The fixed initialization also prevents attributing the depth dependence to initialization under V4. Add the four-epoch training budget.

relationships.condition: 100-layer U(1) and O(4) equivariant radial-tanh MLPs on Fashion-MNIST, evaluated after five epochs
relationships.reason: R1 and R3 show learning beginning when initialization enters the symmetry-broken regime, where a protected Jacobian component remains nonvanishing. This supports initialization-dependent trainability within the fixed budget.
relationships.display_finding: Learning began in the symmetry-broken regime, where a protected Jacobian component remained nonvanishing.

relationships.condition: Generic radial O(4)-activation MLP near its critical initialization, and equivariant MLP initialization sweeps on MNIST
relationships.reason: From text rather than captured rows: Figure 10 reports modest performance gains confined near the generic model's transition; Figure 11 reports the equivariant learning onset in the symmetry-broken regime on MNIST.
relationships.display_finding: Generic radial models showed modest gains confined near their transition, while equivariant MNIST models began learning in the symmetry-broken regime.

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.
